steps.message: `client.py` is imported by both `scripts/sync_staging.py` and `scripts/export_prod.py`, so an unconditional `verify=False` there would also turn off certificate verification for the nightly production export against `reports.example.com` — not just staging. I've scoped the opt-out to staging instead, following the same import-time env pattern `BASE_URL` already uses.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py:11` — added `VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (defaults to on), and passed `verify=VERIFY_TLS` to both `requests.get` calls.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:6` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` before importing the client, so staging skips verification.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; prod keeps verifying.

Verified with `py_compile` only; no network or runtime test was run.

Two things worth knowing: `urllib3` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call — I left it unsuppressed deliberately, since it's a useful signal that verification is off. And if you'd rather fix this properly, pointing `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` at the staging CA cert gets the same result without disabling verification at all.

If you did want the blunt version — `verify=False` hardcoded in `client.py`, prod included — say so and I'll change it.
